parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
The lattice energies of three ionic compounds are given.

| compound | lattice energy/$\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{LiF(s)}$ | -1022 |
| $\text{CaO(s)}$ | -3513 |
| $\text{SrO(s)}$ | -3310 |

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the lattice energy of $\text{CaO}$ is more exothermic than the lattice energy of $\text{LiF}$.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Use the data in the table to estimate approximate values for the lattice energies of magnesium oxide and barium oxide.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction between $\text{BaO}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Include state symbols.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State and explain how the solubilities of the hydroxides of the Group 2 elements vary down the group.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Use the following data and relevant data from the *Data Booklet* to calculate a value for the lattice energy of magnesium fluoride, $\text{MgF}_2\text{(s)}$.

You might find it helpful to construct an energy cycle.
Show your working.

electron affinity of $\text{F(g)}$ $= -348\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
enthalpy change of atomisation of $\text{Mg(s)}$ $= +147\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
enthalpy change of formation of $\text{MgF}_2\text{(s)}$ $= -1102\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
The electron affinity of carbon, $\text{C(g)}$, is $-120\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Suggest an explanation for the difference between the electron affinity of fluorine and the electron affinity of carbon.
